This suggests a potential mechanism where Tenalisib may inhibit the activity of the Dual serine/threonine and tyrosine protein kinase, leading to a downstream effect on RWLeu4. The evidence indicates that Tenalisib could act as a modulator of this kinase, possibly through direct binding or by influencing its activity, which in turn affects RWLeu4. The presence of multiple targets and their shared pathway to RWLeu4 supports a mechanistic link, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
